Opioids.note: The HSE's first bullet under "If you have a challenging experience, you could:" holds both quoted parts. Both The Level bullets begin "If you are able,". The line says no more than these. For the editor, for the whole family: on both The Level pages the "Try:" list follows the milder effects (heroin page: "You might feel nauseous, itchy, tired, disoriented or sedated."); stronger signs go to "a doctor or Healthline", and the signs of an overdose to 111.

On The Level's heroin page the two quoted parts are one bullet; the prescription opioids page has the same bullet with "opioids". The HSE opioids page opened at the www2 address as given (heading "Reducing risks from opioids - Opioids"); the quoted sentence is the first one under "Mixing opioids with alcohol or other drugs".

The Level's bullets say to sit or lie down; the line keeps only sitting, which is less than the sources say, not more. For the editor: the same HSE list also says "Avoid going somewhere else by yourself." Line 0 of this family covers not being alone, so it should stay above this one.
The Level's bullets open with "Focus on breathing"; the HSE bullet opens "pick something else to focus on".
The line keeps the HSE's manner ("in small sips"); the HSE's amount, "a glass of water", is given as "some water". Neither source gives another limit for this family.

Last line of the family, as required. The NHS box is headed "Immediate action required: Call 999 if:" and the line keeps both of its terms. HSE (112 or 999) and The Level (111) confirm the breathing sign. For the editor: "very drowsy" as a reason for an emergency call rests on the NHS methadone page alone; The Level sends "having trouble staying awake" (heroin) and "feeling extremely drowsy" (prescription opioids) to "a doctor or Healthline" and keeps 111 for not being able to wake or stay awake. The line errs toward calling, so it stays.

Stimulants.note: The quoted sentence opens the section "What to do if someone is overamping?" of The Level's story on stimulants (MDMA, meth, coke; December 12th, 2024). The line keeps both of the source's hedges ("mild", "can") and says it for the family the source says it for. One publisher only. For the editor: the same section's water advice, written for helpers, is "some water or a sweet drink to sip slowly".
On both The Level pages the bullet begins "Move to somewhere quiet".
The Level's bullets open with "Focus on breathing"; the HSE bullet opens "pick something else to focus on".
The HSE bullet goes on "- make sure that you are not alone". Both The Level bullets begin "If you are able,".

All three passages are advice for before and during use (ADF "Reducing harm"; HSE advice to people at events; DanceSafe "Basic Tips" under "PREVENTING HEATSTROKE"), not written for the moment it is already too much; the act is the same and the line adds nothing to it. The HSE bullet begins "Keep cool and stay hydrated but don’t drink over a pint of water an hour." DanceSafe's sentence that certain drugs raise the risk stands under the heading "Heatstroke is surprisingly dangerous".

On The Level's amphetamine page the two quoted parts are one bullet; the methamphetamine page has the same bullet with "meth". The HSE sentence is the last one under "If you have a challenging experience".

Last line of the family, as required. All four signs are in The Level's own list under "Call 111 if someone:". "Call an ambulance" is the ADF's own term ("Call triple zero (000) and request an ambulance"); in the ADF list the chest-pain bullet stands under "heart attack symptoms such as:".

Entactogens.note: All four passages are advice for during use (regular breaks), not written for the moment it is already too much; the act is the same. The ADF bullet goes on "this reduces the risk of overheating and can lower heart rate".

The line keeps the limit all four sources give: the manner (HSE "in small sips") and that too much is dangerous (FRANK, ADF, DanceSafe). Its hedge "can" is FRANK's; the ADF says it without a hedge ("is dangerous"). For the editor: the sources also give a ceiling in numbers, which the line leaves out: ADF, in the sentence before the quoted one, "drink around 250-500ml of water per hour"; HSE (about.hse.ie news, an anchor page of line 6) "don’t drink over a pint of water an hour"; FRANK adds "If you drink too quickly you might affect your body's salt balance". The second half of the line is close to FRANK's sentence (seven common words). DanceSafe's heading is numbered on the page: "3. Hydrate and Replenish Electrolytes".

The ADF bullet goes on "so they can help if you’re unwell". DanceSafe's heading is numbered on the page ("1. The Buddy System"), and the same tip says to tell friends what you have taken "so they can help you".
The Level's bullet begins "Move to somewhere quiet". The Loop's sentence begins "Sometimes" and stands under "Setting:".

The HSE bullet goes on "if you are at a festival or an event". FRANK's sentence begins "If you or anyone else starts to feel unwell," ("Tips to stay safe" is plain text, not a heading). The Level's sentence ends "if you need help". For the editor: the line names the medical tent and stands before the family's last line; on the HSE page this bullet is one of the things "you could" do yourself, listed before the heading "Get help if you need it", so the line follows the source's placement.
On The Level page the two quoted parts are one bullet. The HSE sentence is the last one under "If you have a challenging experience".

Entactogens.line: Get medical help without delay for a high temperature, a severe headache, a fit or chest pain.
Entactogens.note: All six anchors are on their pages. The fix is one word: the line said "a very high temperature", but its sources' own terms are "a high fever" (The Level, among the signs of an MDMA overdose, then "Call 111.") and "a high temperature" (HSE). "Very high" sets the point for getting help later than the sources do, so it goes; the line stays the last of the family. For the editor: for a high fever, a fit and chest pain the sources' own action is an emergency call (The Level "Call 111."; HSE "Emergency action required: Phone 112 or 999 if"). "Get medical help without delay" is the HSE's wording for people at events ("Don’t delay getting medical help") and matches DanceSafe's "Seek medical attention" for the headache; it says no more than any source, but it is the milder of the two actions.

Classic psychedelics.note: The ADF has the same sentence under "Bad trips" on all four pages (LSD, psilocybin, DMT, 2C-B), so "not life-threatening" is said for this family, and the line keeps the source's hedge ("generally"). "It will pass" is unhedged in the ADF ("will go away") and the HSE; The Level's DMT page hedges it ("Most of these feelings"). The Level story's bullet goes on "that you're safe and you will be okay". For the editor: the middle of the line follows the ADF's sentence closely (its hedge has to be kept); and The Level adds a caveat the line does not carry, that what you have may not be the drug you think ("isn't actually LSD").

FRANK's sentence begins, on the LSD page, "If you feel that you’re having, or are going to have, a bad trip,"; the mushrooms page (heading "Psylocibin, Psilocin") has it directly under "Duration". The HSE list also has the bullet "tell someone how you feel".

Fireside's section "8. Change The Setting" is one sentence that ends "can radically change your experience" (article heading "10 Safety Practices for Psychedelic Experiences"; the browser title says "Trips"). The HSE psilocybin page opened at the www2 address as given; the quoted sentence follows the bold lead-in "Try to be in a calm place."
The Level's bullets open with "Focus on breathing"; the story's bullet stands in the list after "You could also try:".

The Level's sentence begins "A common tip is that if you begin to feel overwhelmed,": the line keeps its "can" but not that it is a tip people pass on. Fireside gives it in its own voice as a technique to consider ("Radical Acceptance"). The Zendo sentence opens item 3 and is addressed to helpers, as the anchor says.
On The Level page the two quoted parts are one bullet. The HSE sentence is the last one under "If you have a challenging experience".

Last line of the family, as required. Fireside's answer to "Should I call 911 if I'm scared?" is two sentences, and the anchors quote from both; the line keeps the hedge ("does not always"), and its three signs are in the sources' own terms (the HSE bullet goes on "and may be a danger to themselves or others"). For the editor, because this line also says when not to call: (1) its first half rests on Fireside alone; (2) The Level's LSD page, an anchor page of this line, lists "intense feelings of fear that you are dying or going insane" among the signs for "Call 111." (its DMT page says the same), which this line covers only with "panic that will not calm down"; (3) between nothing and an ambulance the sources name a middle step the line leaves out: HSE "The safest thing to do is to get medical advice." and The Level's "call a doctor or Healthline" for a panic attack. The line says no more than its anchors, so it stays.
